Spot.why: the port is code: Lean core, C-Flock's verifier library, the core protocol interface, the LMS verifier (the challenger's signed record) and Lean's hash map (R3's port index, `Registration.portIndex`), no Mathlib and nothing of Security (the layout rule: Lean code never requires Security); Circuits.Wire: the verifier's wire check reads the circuits' one definition of a wire and holds none of its own; Circuits.Wire imports only Lean's own JSON; Circuits.Lanes: SPOT's wiring reads a part's leaves by the circuits' one reader of a part's lanes and holds none of its own; it imports only Circuits.Program; Circuits.DefinitionDigest: the block's circuit file and the pins are read by the circuits' one digest of a Definition's closure and hold none of their own; it imports only the base's bytes, canonical form and hash, and Circuits.Steps; Commitments.SessionCoins: SPOT's supplied values are read through the commitments' one derivation of a session's coins and hold none of their own; it imports only the commitments' Hm96 and frame-v3 and the base's hash and bytes

Spot.RecordText.why: what an execution phase's circuit record's text declares is code, read from the decoded Program and the parsed text alone: Flock's program decoder and template queries, a type's bits read from its structure (Flock.Sigma, which imports the decoder alone) and SPOT's reader of the record's wires, Spot.Edges: the reader's wiring is the Program's edges, and Flock.JsonParse, the total JSON parser its checked examples parse their texts by; code reading the code beneath it; nothing else of SPOT, no Mathlib and nothing of Security
